decisions.choice: the coming kingdom of David: the crowd hopes that God's promise to David's line is about to be fulfilled
decisions.reason: God promised David a son whose kingdom would last forever (2 Samuel 7:12-16). These words are not in Psalm 118. Blind Bartimaeus has just called Jesus "Son of David" (10:47-48), and the crowd now welcomes David's kingdom.

decisions.choice: our father David: David as forefather of the nation
decisions.reason: "Father" is used of a forefather. Israel looked back to David as the founder of its royal line.

decisions.choice: Hosanna in the highest: let the cry be raised in the highest heavens, to God himself
decisions.reason: "The highest" means the heights of heaven, where God is (Psalm 148:1). The crowd calls on God in heaven to hear and act.

decisions.choice: the highest heaven (B, R); to God (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "the highest" refers to. Readable also says "ancestor" for "father".

decisions.choice: "vương quốc" for kingdom; "tổ phụ" (L, B), "tổ tiên" (R) for "father"
decisions.reason: "Vương quốc" is the word the Vietnamese John uses for the kingdom (3:5; 18:36). "Cha" would make David a parent; "tổ phụ" is the Bible word for a forefather of the nation, and Readable uses the everyday "tổ tiên".

decisions.choice: "nơi chí cao" (L); "các tầng trời cao nhất" (B); "trời cao nhất" with "ngợi khen Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the short Bible phrase for "the highest"; Balanced and Readable say plainly that the highest heavens are meant, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "우리 아버지 다윗" (L); "우리 조상 다윗" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek "father"; Balanced and Readable say "조상" (forefather), which is what "father" means here (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: el reino venidero de nuestro padre David
decisions.reason: "El reino que viene de nuestro padre David" could be read as a kingdom coming from David; the adjective keeps the Greek sense.

decisions.choice: le royaume qui vient, [celui] de notre père David
alternatives: le royaume qui vient de notre père David
decisions.reason: Without the supplied pronoun, French "qui vient de" would read "which comes from" David; the bracket keeps the Greek order and its sense.

decisions.choice: o reino ... de Davi, lowercase
decisions.reason: The crowd speaks of the kingdom promised to David's line (m1), not in the phrase "o Reino de Deus", which takes a capital (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 5). Lowercase keeps the crowd's hope in its own terms; the meaning note says what it looked for.

decisions.choice: "በአርያም" (in the highest) (L, B); "በሰማይ ላለው አምላክ" (R)
decisions.reason: "አርያም" is the living church word for the highest heaven, used in praise, and is the word of Matthew 21:9; the Readable says plainly that the cry goes up to God in heaven, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "в вышних" (L); "в высоте небес" (B); "Богу на небесах" (R)
decisions.reason: The same forms as Matthew 21:9 at each level. "Царство" is written small here, since it is David's kingdom the crowd names.

decisions.choice: "हमारे पूर्वज दाऊद" (R); "हमारे पिता दाऊद" (L, B)
decisions.reason: David as forefather of the nation (meaning decision m2): Readable says "ancestor", as the English does; "पूर्वज" needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: "最も高い所で" (L); "天の高みに" (B); "いちばん高い天におられる神に" (R)
decisions.reason: "The highest" means the heights of heaven where God is (m3). Literal keeps the bare phrase; Balanced names heaven and Readable names God, as the English does. The literary "いと高き所" is avoided as a classical form.

source.text: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα εἰς τὸ ἱερόν· καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντα ὀψὲ ἤδη οὔσης τῆς ὥρας ἐξῆλθεν εἰς Βηθανίαν μετὰ τῶν δώδεκα.

records.literal_gloss: And he entered into Jerusalem into the temple, and having looked around at all things, late already being the hour, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered into Jerusalem, into the temple, and having looked around at everything, since the hour was already late, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out to Bethany with the twelve.
en.B: Jesus went into Jerusalem and into the temple courts. He looked all around at everything, but because it was already late in the day, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} left for Bethany with the Twelve.
en.R: Jesus went into Jerusalem and into the temple area. He looked around at everything. But it was already late, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went back to Bethany with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} twelve disciples.

vi.L: Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} vào Giê-ru-sa-lem, vào đền thờ; và sau khi nhìn quanh mọi vật, vì giờ đã muộn, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ra Bê-tha-ni với [nhóm] Mười Hai.
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu vào Giê-ru-sa-lem và vào sân đền thờ. Ngài nhìn quanh mọi thứ, nhưng vì trời đã muộn, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} ra về Bê-tha-ni với nhóm Mười Hai.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu vào Giê-ru-sa-lem và vào sân đền thờ. Ngài nhìn quanh mọi thứ. Nhưng vì trời đã tối, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trở về Bê-tha-ni với mười hai môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 예루살렘으로, 성전 안으로 들어가셨다. 그리고 모든 것을 둘러보신 뒤에, 시간이 이미 늦었으므로 열둘과 함께 베다니로 나가셨다.
ko.B: 예수께서 예루살렘에 들어가 성전 뜰로 가셨다. 그리고 모든 것을 둘러보셨으나, 날이 이미 저물었으므로 열두 제자와 함께 베다니로 나가셨다.
ko.R: 예수께서 예루살렘에 들어가셔서 성전 뜰로 가셨다. 예수께서는 그곳의 모든 것을 둘러보셨다. 그러나 이미 날이 저물었기 때문에, 열두 제자와 함께 베다니로 돌아가셨다.

es.L: Y entró en Jerusalén, en el templo; y, habiendo mirado todo alrededor, siendo ya tarde la hora, salió a Betania con los doce.
es.B: Jesús entró en Jerusalén y fue a los atrios del templo. Miró todo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor, pero, como ya era tarde, se fue a Betania con los Doce.
es.R: Jesús entró en Jerusalén y fue al patio del templo. Miró todo lo que había alrededor. Pero ya era tarde, así que volvió a Betania con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} doce discípulos.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra à Jérusalem, dans le temple ; et ayant regardé tout autour, l’heure étant déjà tardive, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit vers Béthanie avec les douze.
fr.B: Jésus entra dans Jérusalem et alla dans la cour du temple. Il regarda tout autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, mais comme il était déjà tard, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} repartit pour Béthanie avec les Douze.
fr.R: Jésus est entré dans Jérusalem et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est allé dans la cour du temple. Il a tout regardé autour de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Mais il était déjà tard, alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est retourné à Béthanie avec {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} douze disciples.

sw.L: Naye akaingia Yerusalemu, ndani ya hekalu; na akiisha kutazama pande zote vitu vyote, kwa kuwa saa ilikuwa imekwisha kuwa jioni, akatoka kwenda Bethania pamoja na wale kumi na wawili.
sw.B: Yesu aliingia Yerusalemu, akaenda katika nyua za hekalu. Akatazama kila kitu pande zote, lakini kwa kuwa ilikuwa imekwisha kuwa jioni, akaondoka kwenda Bethania pamoja na wale Kumi na Wawili.
sw.R: Yesu aliingia Yerusalemu, akaenda katika eneo la hekalu. Akatazama kila kitu pande zote. Lakini ilikuwa imekwisha kuwa jioni, kwa hiyo akarudi Bethania pamoja na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kumi na wawili.

pt.L: E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} entrou em Jerusalém, no templo; e, depois de olhar tudo ao redor, como a hora já era tarde, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} saiu para Betânia com os Doze.
pt.B: Jesus entrou em Jerusalém e foi aos pátios do templo. Olhou tudo ao redor, mas, como já era tarde, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} saiu para Betânia com os Doze.
pt.R: Jesus entrou em Jerusalém e foi até a área do templo. Ele olhou tudo em volta. Mas já era tarde. Por isso {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} voltou para Betânia com os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} doze discípulos.

am.L: ወደ ኢየሩሳሌምም ወደ ቤተ መቅደስ ገባ፤ ሁሉንም ዙሪያውን ተመልክቶ፣ ሰዓቱም መሽቶ ስለ ነበረ ከአሥራ ሁለቱ ጋር ወደ ቢታንያ ወጣ።
am.B: ኢየሱስ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ገብቶ ወደ ቤተ መቅደሱ አደባባይ ሄደ። ሁሉንም ነገር ዙሪያውን ተመለከተ፤ ነገር ግን ቀኑ መሽቶ ስለ ነበረ ከአሥራ ሁለቱ ጋር ወደ ቢታንያ ወጣ።
am.R: ኢየሱስ ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ገባ፤ ወደ ቤተ መቅደሱ አደባባይም ሄደ። በዚያ ያለውን ሁሉ ዙሪያውን ተመለከተ። ነገር ግን ቀኑ መሽቶ ነበር፤ ስለዚህ ከአሥራ ሁለቱ ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ጋር ወደ ቢታንያ ተመለሰ።

ru.L: И {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} вошёл в Иерусалим, в Храм, и, осмотрев всё, так как час был уже поздний, вышел в Вифанию с двенадцатью.
ru.B: Иисус вошёл в Иерусалим и во двор Храма. Он всё вокруг осмотрел, но так как было уже поздно, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} ушёл в Вифанию с Двенадцатью.
ru.R: Иисус вошёл в Иерусалим и во двор Храма. Он посмотрел вокруг на всё. Но было уже поздно, и {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} вернулся в Вифанию со своими двенадцатью учениками.

hi.L: और वे यरूशलेम में, मन्दिर में गए, और चारों ओर सब कुछ देखकर, क्योंकि घड़ी पहले ही देर की हो चुकी थी, वे बारहों के साथ बाहर बैतनिय्याह को गए।
hi.B: यीशु यरूशलेम में और मन्दिर के आँगन में गए। उन्होंने चारों ओर सब कुछ देखा, पर दिन ढल चुका था, इसलिए वे बारहों के साथ बैतनिय्याह चले गए।
hi.R: यीशु यरूशलेम में और मन्दिर के आँगन में गए। उन्होंने चारों ओर सब कुछ देखा। पर बहुत देर हो चुकी थी, इसलिए वे अपने बारह चेलों के साथ बैतनिय्याह लौट गए।

uk.L: І {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} увійшов у Єрусалим, у храм; і, оглянувши все, оскільки година була вже пізня, вийшов до Віфанії з Дванадцятьма.
uk.B: Ісус увійшов до Єрусалима й до храму. Він оглянув усе довкола, але оскільки було вже пізно, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} пішов до Віфанії з Дванадцятьма.
uk.R: Ісус увійшов до Єрусалима й пішов до храму. Він оглянув там усе. Але було вже пізно, тож {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} повернувся до Віфанії зі своїми дванадцятьма учнями.

ja.L: そして[イエスは]エルサレムに、神殿に入られた。そしてすべてを見回されたが、時刻がすでに遅かったので、十二人と共にベタニアへ出て行かれた。
ja.B: イエスはエルサレムに入り、神殿の境内に入られた。そして辺りのすべてを見回されたが、もう夕方になっていたので、十二人と一緒にベタニアへ出て行かれた。
ja.R: イエスはエルサレムに入って、神殿の境内に行かれました。そして、そこにあるものをすべて見回されました。けれども、もう遅い時間だったので、十二人の弟子たちと一緒にベタニアへ帰って行かれました。

decisions.choice: the temple: the whole temple area with its courts
decisions.reason: The word used here covers the large walled area with its courts and porches. The sanctuary itself, which only priests entered, is called by another word (15:38).

decisions.choice: having looked around at everything: Jesus takes in what is happening there
decisions.reason: He looks, then leaves. What he saw comes to light the next day (11:15-17).

decisions.choice: he went out to Bethany: he lodged outside the city
decisions.reason: At the festivals Jerusalem was crowded with pilgrims, and many stayed in nearby villages. Jesus returns to the city each day (11:15, 11:27).

decisions.choice: the Twelve (B); his twelve disciples (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the number as Mark gives it. Balanced writes it as the name of the group; Readable says who they were.

decisions.choice: "đền thờ" (L); "sân đền thờ" (B, R) for the temple area (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The Greek word means the whole temple precinct with its courts, as in docs/john-terms.md; Balanced and Readable name the courts, where the buying and selling and the teaching took place.

decisions.choice: "[nhóm] Mười Hai" (L); "nhóm Mười Hai" (B)
decisions.reason: Vietnamese cannot use a bare number as a noun, so Literal supplies "nhóm" in brackets; Balanced names the group as a group, as the English "the Twelve" (4:10).

decisions.choice: "성전" (L); "성전 뜰" (B, R) for hieron, through chapters 11-12
decisions.reason: As in the Korean John: hieron is the whole temple area with its courts, so Balanced and Readable say "성전 뜰"; Literal keeps the single word.

decisions.choice: el templo (L); los atrios del templo (B); el patio del templo (R)
decisions.reason: The whole temple area (meaning decision m1), as Spanish John 2:14 renders it. This applies throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: le temple (L); la cour du temple (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in John: this word is the whole temple area with its courts (meaning decision), where Jesus walks, teaches and drives out the traders. Literal keeps "le temple"; Balanced and Readable say "la cour du temple" throughout Mark 11-12.

decisions.choice: "hekalu" (L); "nyua za hekalu" (B); "eneo la hekalu" (R)
decisions.reason: The word is the whole temple area with its courts, as the meaning note says. As in John 2:14, Literal says "hekalu" and Balanced and Readable name the courts or the grounds, so that "hekalu" alone can stand for the sanctuary. The same holds through Mark 11 and 12.

decisions.choice: "ቤተ መቅደሱ አደባባይ" (the temple courts) (B, R); "ቤተ መቅደስ" (L)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the whole temple area (m1), where people walked, bought and taught; "ቤተ መቅደስ" alone suggests the sanctuary building, so Balanced and Readable say its courts, as in Matthew 21:12. The same holds through 11:15-16 and 11:27.

decisions.choice: "Храм" with a capital; "двор Храма" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 21:12: the Temple in Jerusalem takes a capital, and Balanced and Readable say "двор Храма" for the courts where people walked and traded (also 11:15-16, 11:27).

decisions.choice: "मन्दिर के आँगन" (B, R); "मन्दिर" (L)
decisions.reason: The temple here is the whole area with its courts (meaning decision m1), as in Matthew 21:12; Balanced and Readable say so, through this chapter.

decisions.choice: "神殿" (L); "神殿の境内" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word covers the whole walled temple area with its courts (m1). Literal keeps the one word "神殿"; Balanced and Readable say "the temple courts", as the English does, so that the trading of 11:15 is not pictured inside the sanctuary. The sanctuary itself (15:38) is "神殿" at every level. This holds through chapters 11-12.

decisions.choice: "十二人" (L, B); "十二人の弟子たち" (R)
decisions.reason: Japanese "十二人" already works as the name of the group, so Literal and Balanced need no difference; Readable says who they were.

source.text: Καὶ τῇ ἐπαύριον ἐξελθόντων αὐτῶν ἀπὸ Βηθανίας ἐπείνασεν.

records.literal_gloss: And on the next day, having gone out they from Bethany, he was hungry.

en.L: And on the next day, when they had gone out from Bethany, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was hungry.
en.B: The next day, as they were leaving Bethany, Jesus was hungry.
en.R: The next day, as they left Bethany, Jesus became hungry.

vi.L: Và ngày hôm sau, khi họ ra khỏi Bê-tha-ni, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đói.
vi.B: Hôm sau, khi họ rời Bê-tha-ni, Đức Giê-xu thấy đói.
vi.R: Hôm sau, khi họ rời Bê-tha-ni, Đức Giê-xu cảm thấy đói.

ko.L: 그리고 이튿날 그들이 베다니에서 나왔을 때에, 그분이 시장하셨다.
ko.B: 이튿날 그들이 베다니를 떠날 때에, 예수께서 시장하셨다.
ko.R: 다음 날 그들이 베다니를 떠날 때, 예수께서 배가 고프셨다.

es.L: Y al día siguiente, cuando salieron de Betania, tuvo hambre.
es.B: Al día siguiente, cuando salían de Betania, Jesús tuvo hambre.
es.R: Al día siguiente, cuando salían de Betania, Jesús sintió hambre.

fr.L: Et le lendemain, comme ils étaient sortis de Béthanie, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut faim.
fr.B: Le lendemain, comme ils quittaient Béthanie, Jésus eut faim.
fr.R: Le lendemain, quand ils sont partis de Béthanie, Jésus a eu faim.

sw.L: Na siku iliyofuata, walipokuwa wametoka Bethania, aliona njaa.
sw.B: Kesho yake, walipokuwa wakitoka Bethania, Yesu aliona njaa.
sw.R: Kesho yake, walipoondoka Bethania, Yesu alihisi njaa.

pt.L: E, no dia seguinte, quando eles saíram de Betânia, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} teve fome.
pt.B: No dia seguinte, quando saíam de Betânia, Jesus sentiu fome.
pt.R: No dia seguinte, quando eles estavam saindo de Betânia, Jesus ficou com fome.

am.L: በማግሥቱም ከቢታንያ በወጡ ጊዜ ተራበ።
am.B: በማግሥቱ ከቢታንያ ሲወጡ ኢየሱስ ተራበ።
am.R: በማግሥቱ ከቢታንያ ሲወጡ ኢየሱስ ራበው።

ru.L: И на следующий день, когда они вышли из Вифании, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} проголодался.
ru.B: На следующий день, когда они выходили из Вифании, Иисус проголодался.
ru.R: На следующий день, когда они уходили из Вифании, Иисус захотел есть.

hi.L: और अगले दिन, जब वे बैतनिय्याह से निकले, तो उन्हें भूख लगी।
hi.B: अगले दिन, जब वे बैतनिय्याह से निकल रहे थे, तो यीशु को भूख लगी।
hi.R: अगले दिन, जब वे बैतनिय्याह से चले, तो यीशु को भूख लगी।

uk.L: І наступного дня, коли вони вийшли з Віфанії, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} зголоднів.
uk.B: Наступного дня, коли вони виходили з Віфанії, Ісус зголоднів.
uk.R: Наступного дня, коли вони виходили з Віфанії, Ісус захотів їсти.

ja.L: そして翌日、彼らがベタニアから出て来たとき、[イエスは]空腹になられた。
ja.B: 翌日、一行がベタニアを出たとき、イエスは空腹を覚えられた。
ja.R: 次の日、ベタニアを出たとき、イエスはおなかをすかせておられました。

decisions.choice: having gone out from Bethany: they were on the road back to Jerusalem
alternatives: they had already reached the city
decisions.reason: The phrase sets the scene: on the way from Bethany to the city.

decisions.choice: he was hungry: Jesus' real human need
alternatives: a pretense to teach a lesson
decisions.reason: Mark speaks plainly of Jesus' hunger. What follows becomes a sign, but it begins with an ordinary need.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the subject.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν ἀπὸ μακρόθεν ἔχουσαν φύλλα ἦλθεν εἰ ἄρα τι εὑρήσει ἐν αὐτῇ, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐπ’ αὐτὴν οὐδὲν εὗρεν εἰ μὴ φύλλα, ὁ γὰρ καιρὸς οὐκ ἦν σύκων.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen a fig tree from afar having leaves, he went if perhaps anything he will find on it, and having come to it nothing he found except leaves; for the season not was of figs.

en.L: And seeing from a distance a fig tree having leaves, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went [to see] if perhaps {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would find anything on it, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came to it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found nothing except leaves, for it was not [the] season of figs.
en.B: Seeing at a distance a fig tree covered in leaves, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went over to find out whether there was anything on it. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} reached it, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found nothing but leaves, because it was not the time of year for figs.
en.R: In the distance {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw a fig tree with leaves on it. He went to see if it had any fruit. But when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} got there, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} found only leaves. It was not the season for figs.

vi.L: Và từ xa thấy một cây vả có lá, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến [xem] thử có tìm được gì trên cây không; và khi đến nơi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không tìm được gì ngoài lá, vì không phải là mùa vả.
vi.B: Từ xa trông thấy một cây vả đầy lá, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đến xem trên cây có trái nào không. Khi đến nơi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chẳng thấy gì ngoài lá, vì bấy giờ chưa phải mùa vả.
vi.R: Từ xa, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thấy một cây vả có lá. Ngài đến xem cây có trái không. Nhưng khi đến nơi, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chỉ thấy lá. Lúc ấy chưa phải mùa vả.

ko.L: 그리고 멀리서 잎이 난 무화과나무 한 그루를 보시고, 혹시 그 나무에서 무엇을 찾으실까 하여 가셨다. 그러나 그 나무에 가셔서 잎사귀 말고는 아무것도 찾지 못하셨다. 무화과의 철이 아니었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 예수께서는 멀리서 잎이 무성한 무화과나무 한 그루를 보시고, 혹시 열매가 있을까 하여 가까이 가 보셨다. 그러나 가서 보니 잎사귀밖에 없었다. 무화과가 열릴 철이 아니었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 멀리 있는 무화과나무 한 그루를 보셨다. 그 나무에는 잎이 나 있었다. 예수께서는 열매가 있는지 보러 가셨다. 그러나 가까이 가 보니 잎만 있었다. 아직 무화과가 열릴 때가 아니었다.

es.L: Y viendo de lejos una higuera que tenía hojas, fue [a ver] si acaso encontraba algo en ella; y al llegar a ella no encontró nada sino hojas, porque no era [el] tiempo de [los] higos.
es.B: Vio a lo lejos una higuera cubierta de hojas y se acercó para ver si tenía algo. Cuando llegó, no encontró más que hojas, porque no era la temporada de los higos.
es.R: Desde lejos vio una higuera con hojas. Fue a ver si tenía algún higo. Pero cuando llegó, solo encontró hojas. No era la temporada de los higos.

fr.L: Et voyant de loin un figuier qui avait des feuilles, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} alla [voir] si par hasard {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} y trouverait quelque chose ; et étant arrivé près de lui, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne trouva rien que des feuilles, car ce n’était pas la saison des figues.
fr.B: Voyant de loin un figuier couvert de feuilles, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’approcha pour voir s’il y avait quelque chose dessus. Arrivé près de l’arbre, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne trouva que des feuilles, car ce n’était pas la saison des figues.
fr.R: De loin, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a vu un figuier qui avait des feuilles. Il est allé voir s’il y avait des fruits. Mais quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est arrivé près de l’arbre, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’a trouvé que des feuilles. Ce n’était pas la saison des figues.

sw.L: Na alipouona kwa mbali mtini wenye majani, alikwenda [kuona] kama labda angepata kitu chochote juu yake; na alipoufikia hakupata kitu ila majani, kwa maana haukuwa wakati wa tini.
sw.B: Aliona kwa mbali mtini uliojaa majani, akaenda kuona kama ungekuwa na chochote. Alipoufikia hakukuta kitu ila majani tu, kwa sababu haukuwa msimu wa tini.
sw.R: Kwa mbali aliona mtini wenye majani. Akaenda kuona kama ulikuwa na matunda yoyote. Lakini alipofika, alikuta majani tu. Haukuwa msimu wa tini.

pt.L: E, vendo de longe uma figueira que tinha folhas, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} foi [ver] se porventura encontraria alguma coisa nela; e, quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} chegou até ela, não encontrou nada além de folhas, pois não era [o] tempo de figos.
pt.B: Vendo de longe uma figueira coberta de folhas, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} foi até lá para ver se havia alguma coisa nela. Quando chegou, não encontrou nada além de folhas, porque não era a época dos figos.
pt.R: De longe, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} viu uma figueira com folhas. Foi até lá para ver se ela tinha algum fruto. Mas, quando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} chegou, só encontrou folhas. Não era a época dos figos.

am.L: ከሩቅም ቅጠል ያላትን በለስ አይቶ ምናልባት አንዳች ያገኝባት እንደ ሆነ [ለማየት] መጣ፤ ወደ እርሷም በመጣ ጊዜ ከቅጠል በቀር ምንም አላገኘም፤ የበለስ ወራት አልነበረምና።
am.B: ቅጠል የሞላባትን በለስ ከሩቅ አይቶ አንዳች ይገኝባት እንደ ሆነ ለማየት ወደ እርሷ ሄደ። በደረሰም ጊዜ ከቅጠል በቀር ምንም አላገኘም፤ የበለስ ፍሬ የሚገኝበት ወቅት አልነበረምና።
am.R: ከሩቅ ቅጠል ያላት አንዲት በለስ አየ። ፍሬ ይኖራት እንደ ሆነ ለማየት ሄደ። እዚያ ሲደርስ ግን ቅጠል ብቻ አገኘ። የበለስ ወቅት አልነበረም።

ru.L: И, увидев издали смоковницу, покрытую листьями, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} пошёл [посмотреть], не найдёт ли чего-нибудь на ней, и, подойдя к ней, ничего не нашёл, кроме листьев, ведь было не время смокв.
ru.B: Увидев издали смоковницу, покрытую листьями, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} подошёл посмотреть, нет ли на ней чего-нибудь. Но, подойдя, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} не нашёл ничего, кроме листьев, потому что было не время для инжира.
ru.R: Издали {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} увидел инжировое дерево с листьями. Он пошёл посмотреть, есть ли на нём плоды. Но когда {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} подошёл, то нашёл только листья. Это было не время для инжира.

hi.L: और दूर से पत्तों से लदा अंजीर का एक पेड़ देखकर वे [यह देखने] गए कि शायद उस पर कुछ पाएँ, और उसके पास आकर उन्होंने पत्तों के सिवा कुछ नहीं पाया, क्योंकि यह अंजीरों का मौसम नहीं था।
hi.B: दूर से पत्तों से भरा अंजीर का एक पेड़ देखकर वे यह जानने के लिए उसके पास गए कि उस पर कुछ है या नहीं। पर जब वे वहाँ पहुँचे, तो उन्हें पत्तों के सिवा कुछ नहीं मिला, क्योंकि यह अंजीरों का मौसम नहीं था।
hi.R: उन्होंने दूर से अंजीर का एक पेड़ देखा, जिस पर पत्ते थे। वे यह देखने गए कि उस पर कोई फल है या नहीं। पर जब वे वहाँ पहुँचे, तो उन्हें केवल पत्ते मिले। यह अंजीरों का मौसम नहीं था।

uk.L: І, побачивши здалека смоковницю, що мала листя, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} підійшов [подивитися], чи не знайде чогось на ній; і, підійшовши до неї, нічого не знайшов, крім листя, бо не була пора смокв.
uk.B: Побачивши здалека смоковницю, вкриту листям, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} підійшов, щоб подивитися, чи є на ній щось. Коли {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} підійшов до неї, то не знайшов нічого, крім листя, бо була не пора для інжиру.
uk.R: Здалеку {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} побачив інжир із листям. Він підійшов подивитися, чи є на ньому плоди. Але коли {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} підійшов, то знайшов тільки листя. Була не пора для інжиру.

ja.L: そして遠くから葉のあるいちじくの木を見て、もしかしたら何かその上に見つかるかと[見に]行かれた。そしてそこに来られたが、葉のほかには何も見つけられなかった。いちじくの季節ではなかったからである。
ja.B: 遠くに葉の茂ったいちじくの木が見えたので、何かなっていないかと近寄って行かれた。しかし、そばまで来てみると、葉のほかには何もなかった。いちじくの実のなる季節ではなかったからである。
ja.R: 遠くに、葉のついたいちじくの木が見えました。イエスは、実がなっていないか見に行かれました。でも、そこに着いてみると、葉しかありませんでした。いちじくの実がなる季節ではなかったのです。

decisions.choice: it was not the season for figs: Passover came in spring, and figs ripen in summer
alternatives: the figs had already been picked
decisions.reason: The main fig harvest came in late summer. In spring a fig tree puts out small early fruit with its leaves, so leaves might suggest there was something to eat. This tree had leaves but nothing on it.

decisions.choice: for: Mark explains why there were no figs
alternatives: Mark explains why Jesus went to look
decisions.reason: The note answers the reader's question why the tree was bare. It also shows that the curse that follows is more than a complaint about fruit.

decisions.choice: the fig tree: in the prophets a picture of Israel, and of God finding no fruit among his people
decisions.reason: God compares Israel to early figs (Hosea 9:10) and complains of finding no figs on the tree (Jeremiah 8:13; Micah 7:1). Mark places the temple scene between the two halves of this story (11:12-14; 11:20-21), so each explains the other.

decisions.choice: any fruit
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus was looking for.

decisions.choice: "cây vả" for the fig tree (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: "Cây vả" is the established Bible name for the fig, used in the Vietnamese John (1:48); "cây sung" is a related local tree whose fruit grows on the trunk, which would mislead.

decisions.choice: "በለስ" referred to and addressed in the feminine ("እርሷ", "አንቺ")
decisions.reason: Amharic usually treats a tree spoken to or about in this way as feminine, as Matthew 21:19 does; the curse in 11:14 is addressed to it as "አንቺ".

decisions.choice: "смоковница" (L, B), "инжировое дерево" (R); "смоквы" (L), "инжир" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Смоковница" is the Bible word for the tree and stays at Literal and Balanced; the fruit is now called "инжир". Readable uses the everyday words for both.

decisions.choice: tree "смоковниця" (L, B), "інжир" (R); fruit "смокви" (L), "інжир" (B, R), through 11:13-21
decisions.reason: The brief's Gospel convention: the traditional tree name where readers know it, the everyday name for the fruit.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Μηκέτι εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἐκ σοῦ μηδεὶς καρπὸν φάγοι.

records.literal_gloss: And answering he said to it, No longer into the age from you no one fruit may eat.

en.L: And answering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to it, "May no one eat fruit from you any longer, forever."
en.B: He told the tree, "Let no one eat fruit from you ever again."
en.R: Jesus said to the tree, "From now on, may no one ever eat your fruit again!"

vi.L: Và đáp lại, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói với cây ấy: "Từ nay cho đến đời đời, chớ có ai ăn trái của ngươi nữa!"
vi.B: Ngài nói với cây vả: "Đừng bao giờ còn ai ăn trái của ngươi nữa!"
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu nói với cây vả: "Từ nay trở đi, sẽ không bao giờ có ai được ăn trái của ngươi nữa!"

ko.L: 그러자 그분이 대답하여 그 나무에게 말씀하셨다. "이제부터 영원히 아무도 너에게서 열매를 먹지 못하기를!"
ko.B: 예수께서 그 나무에게 말씀하셨다. "이제부터 다시는 아무도 너에게서 열매를 따 먹지 못할 것이다!"
ko.R: 예수께서 그 나무에게 말씀하셨다. "이제부터 아무도 다시는 네 열매를 먹지 못할 것이다!"

es.L: Y, respondiendo, le dijo: «Que nadie coma ya nunca más fruto de ti».
es.B: Le dijo a la higuera: «¡Que nadie vuelva a comer jamás fruto de ti!».
es.R: Jesús le dijo al árbol: «¡Que desde ahora nadie vuelva a comer nunca tus frutos!».

fr.L: Et en réponse, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Que plus jamais, à tout jamais, personne ne mange de fruit de toi ! »
fr.B: Il dit à l’arbre : « Que plus personne ne mange jamais de ton fruit ! »
fr.R: Jésus a dit à l’arbre : « Désormais, que personne ne mange plus jamais de tes fruits ! »

sw.L: Na akijibu, akauambia, "Mtu yeyote asile tena tunda kutoka kwako hata milele."
sw.B: Akauambia mti, "Mtu yeyote asile tena tunda lako kamwe."
sw.R: Yesu akauambia mti, "Tangu sasa mtu yeyote asile tunda lako tena kamwe!"

pt.L: E, respondendo, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse a ela: "Que ninguém mais coma fruto de você, para sempre."
pt.B: Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} disse à árvore: "Que ninguém nunca mais coma fruto de você."
pt.R: Jesus disse à árvore: "De agora em diante, que ninguém nunca mais coma do seu fruto!"

am.L: መልሶም እንዲህ አላት፦ «ከእንግዲህ ወዲህ ለዘላለም ማንም ከአንቺ ፍሬ አይብላ።»
am.B: ዛፊቱንም «ከእንግዲህ ማንም ከአንቺ ፍሬ ፈጽሞ አይብላ» አላት።
am.R: ኢየሱስም ዛፊቱን «ከአሁን ጀምሮ ማንም ፍሬሽን ፈጽሞ አይብላ!» አላት።

ru.L: И, отвечая, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} сказал ей: «Пусть же никто больше вовек не ест от тебя плода.»
ru.B: Он сказал дереву: «Пусть никто больше никогда не ест от тебя плодов.»
ru.R: Иисус сказал дереву: «Пусть с этих пор никто никогда больше не ест твоих плодов!»

hi.L: और उन्होंने उत्तर में उससे कहा, "अब से युग-युग तक कोई तुम्हारा फल कभी न खाए।"
hi.B: उन्होंने पेड़ से कहा, "अब से कोई तुम्हारा फल फिर कभी न खाए।"
hi.R: यीशु ने पेड़ से कहा, "अब से कोई भी तुम्हारा फल फिर कभी न खाए!"

uk.L: І, відповідаючи, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} сказав їй: «Хай ніхто вже повіки не їсть із тебе плоду.»
uk.B: Він сказав дереву: «Хай ніхто більше ніколи не їсть із тебе плодів.»
uk.R: Ісус сказав дереву: «Відтепер хай ніхто ніколи не їсть твоїх плодів!»

ja.L: そして[イエスは]答えて、それに言われた。「もはや永遠に、だれもおまえから実を食べることがないように。」
ja.B: イエスはその木に言われた。「今後いつまでも、だれもおまえの実を食べることがないように。」
ja.R: イエスはその木に言われました。「これから先、だれも二度とおまえの実を食べることがないように！」

decisions.choice: may no one eat: a wish, spoken as a curse
alternatives: a prediction that no one will eat
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form used for wishes. Peter later calls it a curse (11:21).

decisions.choice: no longer, into the age: never again
alternatives: not for an age, for a long time
decisions.reason: "Into the age" means forever. With "no longer" it makes a strong never again.

decisions.choice: answering: responding to what he found
decisions.reason: No one has spoken. The word introduces Jesus' response to the bare tree.

decisions.choice: the curse is a sign of judgment
decisions.reason: Like the acted signs of the prophets (Jeremiah 19:1-11), the curse on the fruitless tree points to God's judgment, which Jesus goes on to speak of in the temple.

decisions.choice: ever ... again
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable join the two phrases into a natural never again.

decisions.choice: "ngươi" for the tree addressed
decisions.reason: "Ngươi" is the solemn form for an address that pronounces a sentence, as the Vietnamese John uses it for a prophetic address (12:15); "mày" would sound like everyday contempt.

decisions.choice: A future of judgment ("먹지 못할 것이다") for the Greek wish (B, R); the wish form at Literal ("먹지 못하기를")
decisions.reason: The Greek is a wish spoken as a curse (meaning decision). A Korean wish ending sounds like a prayer rather than a sentence passed on the tree; Balanced and Readable give the force of the curse with a solemn future, and Literal keeps the wish.

decisions.choice: você
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 21:19: Jesus addresses the tree as he would one hearer, with "você" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); "tu" is kept for words addressed to God or Jesus.

decisions.choice: "तुम्हारा" to the tree
decisions.reason: Jesus says "तुम" to whatever he addresses (style guide section 4), as to the fig tree in Matthew 21:19.

decisions.choice: "おまえ" for the tree (every level)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to the tree directly, and a curse is said in the plain second person. "おまえ" is the ordinary pronoun for speaking down to a thing or an animal; "あなた" would sound like courtesy.

source.text: καὶ ἤκουον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And were listening the disciples of him.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples were listening.
en.B: And {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples heard it.
en.R: His disciples heard {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} say this.

vi.L: Và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang nghe.
vi.B: Các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đều nghe thấy.
vi.R: Các môn đồ nghe {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói như vậy.

ko.L: 그리고 그분의 제자들이 듣고 있었다.
ko.B: 그분의 제자들도 그 말씀을 들었다.
ko.R: 예수의 제자들도 예수께서 하시는 이 말씀을 들었다.

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos [lo] estaban escuchando.
es.B: Y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos lo oyeron.
es.R: Sus discípulos {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} oyeron decir esto.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples écoutaient.
fr.B: Et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples l’entendirent.
fr.R: Ses disciples {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont entendu dire cela.

sw.L: Na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walikuwa wakisikiliza.
sw.B: Nao wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walisikia.
sw.R: Wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} walimsikia akisema hivyo.

pt.L: E os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos ouviam.
pt.B: E os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos ouviram isso.
pt.R: Os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} ouviram dizer isso.

am.L: ደቀ መዛሙርቱም ይሰሙ ነበር።
am.B: ደቀ መዛሙርቱም ይህን ሰሙ።
am.R: ደቀ መዛሙርቱም ይህን ሲናገር ሰሙት።

ru.L: И слышали [это] {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} ученики.
ru.B: И {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} ученики слышали это.
ru.R: Его ученики слышали, как {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} это сказал.

hi.L: और उनके चेले सुन रहे थे।
hi.B: और उनके चेलों ने यह सुना।
hi.R: उनके चेलों ने उन्हें यह कहते सुना।

uk.L: І {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} учні слухали.
uk.B: І {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} учні чули це.
uk.R: Його учні чули, як {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} це сказав.

ja.L: そして弟子たちは聞いていた。
ja.B: 弟子たちはこれを聞いていた。
ja.R: 弟子たちは、イエスがそう言われるのを聞いていました。

decisions.choice: were listening: the disciples heard the words
decisions.reason: The note prepares for 11:20-21, when Peter remembers what Jesus said.

decisions.choice: heard him say this
decisions.reason: Readable says what they heard.

source.text: Καὶ ἔρχονται εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.

records.literal_gloss: And they come to Jerusalem.

en.L: And they come to Jerusalem.
en.B: Then they came into Jerusalem.
en.R: Then they arrived in Jerusalem.

vi.L: Và họ đến Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.B: Rồi họ vào Giê-ru-sa-lem.
vi.R: Sau đó họ đến Giê-ru-sa-lem.

ko.L: 그리고 그들이 예루살렘으로 온다.
ko.B: 그리고 그들은 예루살렘으로 들어갔다.
ko.R: 그다음에 그들은 예루살렘에 도착했다.

es.L: Y llegan a Jerusalén.
es.B: Luego llegaron a Jerusalén.
es.R: Después llegaron a Jerusalén.

fr.L: Et ils viennent à Jérusalem.
fr.B: Puis ils arrivèrent à Jérusalem.
fr.R: Puis ils sont arrivés à Jérusalem.

sw.L: Na wanakuja Yerusalemu.
sw.B: Kisha wakaingia Yerusalemu.
sw.R: Kisha wakafika Yerusalemu.

pt.L: E chegam a Jerusalém.
pt.B: Então chegaram a Jerusalém.
pt.R: Depois eles chegaram a Jerusalém.

am.L: ወደ ኢየሩሳሌምም ይመጣሉ።
am.B: ከዚያም ወደ ኢየሩሳሌም ገቡ።
am.R: ከዚያም ኢየሩሳሌም ደረሱ።

ru.L: И приходят в Иерусалим.
ru.B: Потом они пришли в Иерусалим.
ru.R: Потом они пришли в Иерусалим.

hi.L: और वे यरूशलेम में आते हैं।
hi.B: फिर वे यरूशलेम में आए।
hi.R: फिर वे यरूशलेम पहुँचे।

uk.L: І приходять до Єрусалима.
uk.B: Потім вони прийшли до Єрусалима.
uk.R: Потім вони прибули до Єрусалима.

ja.L: そして彼らはエルサレムに来る。
ja.B: それから一行はエルサレムに着いた。
ja.R: それから一行は、エルサレムに着きました。

decisions.choice: they come: present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Mark again uses the present for vividness; the sense is past.

decisions.choice: Then
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the step in the story.

decisions.choice: present "来る" (L); past "着いた" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Mark tells a past event in the present tense (m1). Literal keeps the Japanese present, Balanced and Readable narrate in the past, as in 11:1-11. This holds for the historic presents in 11:15-33.

source.text: καὶ εἰσελθὼν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν ἤρξατο ἐκβάλλειν τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ τοὺς ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστερὰς κατέστρεψεν καὶ οὐκ ἤφιεν ἵνα τις διενέγκῃ σκεῦος διὰ τοῦ ἱεροῦ, καὶ ἐδίδασκεν καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Οὐ γέγραπται ὅτι Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν;

records.literal_gloss: And having entered into the temple he began to cast out those selling and those buying in the temple, and the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves he overturned, \v 16 and not he would allow that anyone should carry a vessel through the temple, \v 17 and he was teaching and saying to them, Not has it been written that The house of me a house of prayer will be called for all the nations?

en.L: And entering into the temple, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to cast out those selling and those buying in the temple, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves, \v 16 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not allow anyone to carry a vessel through the temple. \v 17 And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching and saying to them, "Is it not written, 'My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations'?
en.B: He went into the temple courts and began driving out the people who were selling and buying there. He turned over the money changers' tables and the benches of the dove sellers, \v 16 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not let anyone carry goods through the temple courts. \v 17 Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught them, saying, "Does Scripture not say, 'My house will be known as a house of prayer for all the nations'?
en.R: Jesus went into the temple area. He began to throw out the people who were buying and selling things there. He turned over the tables where people exchanged money. He also turned over the seats of those who sold doves. \v 16 He would not let anyone carry things through the temple courts. \v 17 Then Jesus taught the people. He said, "In the Scriptures God says, 'My house will be called a house where people from every nation can pray.'

vi.L: Và vào đền thờ, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bắt đầu đuổi những người bán và những người mua trong đền thờ ra, và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} lật đổ bàn của những người đổi tiền và ghế của những người bán bồ câu, \v 16 và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} không cho ai mang đồ vật gì đi ngang qua đền thờ. \v 17 Và {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dạy dỗ và nói với họ: "Chẳng phải có chép rằng: 'Nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được gọi là nhà cầu nguyện cho mọi dân tộc' sao?
vi.B: Ngài vào sân đền thờ và bắt đầu đuổi những người đang mua bán ở đó ra. Ngài lật đổ bàn của những người đổi tiền và ghế của những người bán bồ câu, \v 16 và không cho ai mang hàng hóa đi ngang qua sân đền thờ. \v 17 Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dạy họ: "Chẳng phải Kinh Thánh đã chép: 'Nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được gọi là nhà cầu nguyện cho mọi dân tộc' sao?
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu vào sân đền thờ. Ngài bắt đầu đuổi những người đang mua bán ở đó ra ngoài. Ngài lật đổ những cái bàn của những người đổi tiền. Ngài cũng lật đổ ghế của những người bán bồ câu. \v 16 Ngài không cho ai mang đồ đạc đi ngang qua sân đền thờ. \v 17 Rồi Đức Giê-xu dạy dân chúng. Ngài nói: "Trong Kinh Thánh, Đức Chúa Trời phán: 'Nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ được gọi là nơi người thuộc mọi dân tộc đến cầu nguyện.'

ko.L: 그리고 그분이 성전에 들어가셔서, 성전 안에서 파는 사람들과 사는 사람들을 쫓아내기 시작하셨고, 돈 바꾸는 사람들의 탁자들과 비둘기 파는 사람들의 의자들을 뒤엎으셨다. \v 16 그리고 아무도 성전을 가로질러 물건을 나르지 못하게 하셨다. \v 17 그리고 가르치시며 그들에게 말씀하셨다. "'내 집은 모든 민족을 위한 기도하는 집이라 불릴 것이다' 하고 기록되어 있지 않으냐?
ko.B: 예수께서 성전 뜰에 들어가셔서, 거기서 물건을 팔고 사는 사람들을 쫓아내기 시작하셨다. 돈 바꾸어 주는 사람들의 탁자와 비둘기 파는 사람들의 의자를 둘러엎으셨고, \v 16 아무도 물건을 들고 성전 뜰을 지나다니지 못하게 하셨다. \v 17 그리고 그들을 가르치며 말씀하셨다. "성경에 '내 집은 모든 민족이 와서 기도하는 집이라 불릴 것이다' 하고 기록되어 있지 않으냐?
ko.R: 예수께서 성전 뜰에 들어가셨다. 그리고 거기서 물건을 사고파는 사람들을 내쫓기 시작하셨다. 예수께서는 사람들에게 돈을 바꾸어 주던 사람들의 탁자를 엎으셨다. 비둘기를 팔던 사람들의 의자도 엎으셨다. \v 16 또 아무도 물건을 들고 성전 뜰을 지나가지 못하게 하셨다. \v 17 그리고 예수께서 사람들을 가르치셨다. 예수께서 말씀하셨다. "성경에서 하나님께서 이렇게 말씀하셨다. '내 집은 모든 나라 사람들이 와서 기도하는 집이라고 불릴 것이다.'

es.L: Y entrando en el templo, comenzó a echar fuera a los que vendían y a los que compraban en el templo, y volcó las mesas de los cambistas y los asientos de los que vendían las palomas, \v 16 y no permitía que nadie llevara objeto alguno a través del templo. \v 17 Y enseñaba y les decía: «¿No está escrito: “Mi casa será llamada casa de oración para todas las naciones”?
es.B: Entró en los atrios del templo y comenzó a expulsar a los que vendían y compraban allí. Volcó las mesas de los cambistas y los puestos de los que vendían palomas, \v 16 y no dejaba que nadie atravesara los atrios del templo cargando mercancías. \v 17 Luego se puso a enseñarles, diciendo: «¿No dice la Escritura: “Mi casa será conocida como casa de oración para todas las naciones”?
es.R: Jesús entró en el patio del templo. Comenzó a echar a la gente que compraba y vendía cosas allí. Volcó las mesas donde la gente cambiaba dinero. También volcó los asientos de los que vendían palomas. \v 16 No dejaba que nadie pasara por el patio del templo cargando cosas. \v 17 Luego Jesús enseñó a la gente. Les dijo: «En las Escrituras Dios dice: “Mi casa será una casa donde gente de todas las naciones pueda orar”.

fr.L: Et étant entré dans le temple, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} commença à chasser ceux qui vendaient et ceux qui achetaient dans le temple, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} renversa les tables des changeurs et les sièges de ceux qui vendaient les colombes, \v 16 et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne laissait personne transporter un objet à travers le temple. \v 17 Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseignait et leur disait : « N’est-il pas écrit : “Ma maison sera appelée maison de prière pour toutes les nations” ?
fr.B: Il entra dans la cour du temple et se mit à chasser ceux qui y vendaient et y achetaient. Il renversa les tables des changeurs et les bancs des marchands de colombes, \v 16 et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne laissait personne traverser la cour du temple en portant des marchandises. \v 17 Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les enseigna en disant : « L’Écriture ne dit-elle pas : “Ma maison sera appelée une maison de prière pour toutes les nations” ?
fr.R: Jésus est entré dans la cour du temple. Il a commencé à chasser les gens qui vendaient et achetaient des choses à cet endroit. Il a renversé les tables de ceux qui changeaient l’argent. Il a aussi renversé les sièges des vendeurs de colombes. \v 16 Il ne laissait personne traverser la cour du temple en portant des affaires. \v 17 Puis Jésus a enseigné les gens. Il leur a dit : « Dans les Écritures, Dieu dit : “Ma maison sera appelée une maison où les gens de toutes les nations pourront prier.”

sw.L: Na alipoingia hekaluni alianza kuwafukuza wale waliokuwa wakiuza na wale waliokuwa wakinunua hekaluni, na akazipindua meza za wabadilishaji fedha na viti vya wale waliokuwa wakiuza njiwa, \v 16 wala hakumruhusu mtu yeyote kubeba chombo kupitia hekaluni. \v 17 Naye alikuwa akifundisha na kuwaambia, "Je, haijaandikwa, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itaitwa nyumba ya maombi kwa ajili ya mataifa yote'?
sw.B: Aliingia katika nyua za hekalu, akaanza kuwafukuza watu waliokuwa wakiuza na kununua humo. Akazipindua meza za wabadilishaji fedha na viti vya wauza njiwa, \v 16 wala hakumruhusu mtu yeyote kupitisha mizigo katika nyua za hekalu. \v 17 Kisha akawafundisha, akisema, "Je, Maandiko hayasemi, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itajulikana kuwa nyumba ya maombi ya mataifa yote'?
sw.R: Yesu aliingia katika eneo la hekalu. Akaanza kuwatoa nje watu waliokuwa wakinunua na kuuza vitu humo. Akazipindua meza za watu waliobadilisha fedha. Akapindua pia viti vya wale waliouza njiwa. \v 16 Hakumruhusu mtu yeyote kubeba vitu kupitia uwanja wa hekalu. \v 17 Kisha Yesu akawafundisha watu. Akasema, "Katika Maandiko Mungu anasema, 'Nyumba {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} itaitwa nyumba ambamo watu wa kila taifa wanaweza kuomba.'

pt.L: E, entrando no templo, {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} começou a expulsar os que vendiam e os que compravam no templo, e derrubou as mesas dos cambistas e as cadeiras dos que vendiam as pombas, \v 16 e não permitia que alguém carregasse um objeto através do templo. \v 17 E {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ensinava e lhes dizia: "Não está escrito: 'Minha casa será chamada casa de oração para todas as nações'?
pt.B: Ele entrou nos pátios do templo e começou a expulsar as pessoas que vendiam e compravam ali. Derrubou as mesas dos cambistas e as cadeiras dos vendedores de pombas, \v 16 e não deixava ninguém atravessar os pátios do templo carregando mercadorias. \v 17 Então {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} os ensinou, dizendo: "As Escrituras não dizem: 'Minha casa será conhecida como casa de oração para todas as nações'?
pt.R: Jesus entrou na área do templo. Ele começou a expulsar as pessoas que estavam comprando e vendendo coisas ali. Derrubou as mesas dos homens que trocavam dinheiro. Também derrubou as cadeiras das pessoas que vendiam pombas. \v 16 Ele não deixava ninguém carregar coisas pelos pátios do templo. \v 17 Então Jesus ensinou o povo. Ele disse: "Nas Escrituras Deus diz: 'Minha casa será chamada uma casa onde pessoas de todas as nações podem orar.'

am.L: ወደ ቤተ መቅደስም ገብቶ በቤተ መቅደስ የሚሸጡትንና የሚገዙትን ያስወጣ ጀመር፤ የገንዘብ ለዋጮችንም ገበታዎች ርግቦችንም የሚሸጡትን ሰዎች ወንበሮች ገለበጠ፤ \v 16 ማንም ዕቃ ይዞ በቤተ መቅደስ ውስጥ እንዲያልፍ አይፈቅድም ነበር። \v 17 ያስተምርም ነበር፤ እንዲህም ይላቸው ነበር፦ «“ቤቴ ለአሕዛብ ሁሉ የጸሎት ቤት ይባላል” ተብሎ አልተጻፈምን?
am.B: ወደ ቤተ መቅደሱ አደባባይ ገብቶ በዚያ የሚሸጡትንና የሚገዙትን ያባርር ጀመር። የገንዘብ ለዋጮችን ጠረጴዛዎችና የርግብ ሻጮችን ወንበሮች ገለበጠ፤ \v 16 ማንም ሰው ዕቃ ተሸክሞ በቤተ መቅደሱ አደባባይ እንዲያልፍ አይፈቅድም ነበር። \v 17 ከዚያም እንዲህ እያለ አስተማራቸው፦ «መጻሕፍት “ቤቴ ለአሕዛብ ሁሉ የጸሎት ቤት ይባላል” አይሉምን?
am.R: ኢየሱስ ወደ ቤተ መቅደሱ አደባባይ ገባ። በዚያ የሚገዙትንና የሚሸጡትን ሰዎች ያስወጣ ጀመር። ገንዘብ የሚለውጡትን ሰዎች ጠረጴዛዎች ገለበጠ። ርግብ የሚሸጡትንም ሰዎች ወንበሮች ገለበጠ። \v 16 ማንም ሰው ዕቃ ይዞ በቤተ መቅደሱ አደባባይ እንዲያልፍ አልፈቀደም። \v 17 ከዚያም ኢየሱስ ሕዝቡን አስተማረ። እንዲህም አለ፦ «እግዚአብሔር በመጻሕፍት “ቤቴ ከሕዝቦች ሁሉ የመጡ ሰዎች የሚጸልዩበት ቤት ይባላል” ይላል።

ru.L: И, войдя в Храм, {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} начал изгонять продающих и покупающих в Храме, и опрокинул столы менял и скамьи продающих голубей, \v 16 и не позволял, чтобы кто-нибудь пронёс вещь через Храм. \v 17 И {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} учил и говорил им: «Разве не написано: “Дом {{deity_pronoun:мой|Мой}} назовётся домом молитвы для всех народов”?
ru.B: Он вошёл во двор Храма и начал выгонять тех, кто там продавал и покупал. Он опрокинул столы менял и скамьи продавцов голубей \v 16 и не позволял никому проносить вещи через двор Храма. \v 17 Потом {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} стал учить их и сказал: «Разве не сказано в Писании: “Мой дом будет назван домом молитвы для всех народов”?
ru.R: Иисус вошёл во двор Храма. Он начал выгонять оттуда людей, которые там покупали и продавали. Он опрокинул столы, за которыми люди меняли деньги. Он опрокинул и скамьи тех, кто продавал голубей. \v 16 Он не позволял никому проносить вещи через двор Храма. \v 17 Потом Иисус стал учить людей. Он сказал: «В Писании Бог говорит: “Мой дом будут называть домом, где люди из всех народов могут молиться.”

hi.L: और मन्दिर में प्रवेश करके वे उन्हें बाहर निकालने लगे जो मन्दिर में बेच रहे थे और ख़रीद रहे थे, और उन्होंने सर्राफ़ों की मेज़ें और कबूतर बेचनेवालों की चौकियाँ उलट दीं, \v 16 और वे किसी को मन्दिर में से होकर कोई बरतन ले जाने नहीं देते थे। \v 17 और वे उपदेश देते हुए उनसे कहने लगे, "क्या यह नहीं लिखा है, 'मेरा घर सब जातियों के लिए प्रार्थना का घर कहलाएगा'?
hi.B: वे मन्दिर के आँगन में गए और वहाँ ख़रीदने-बेचनेवालों को बाहर खदेड़ने लगे। उन्होंने सर्राफ़ों की मेज़ें और कबूतर बेचनेवालों की चौकियाँ उलट दीं, \v 16 और किसी को भी मन्दिर के आँगन में से होकर सामान ले जाने नहीं दिया। \v 17 फिर वे उन्हें उपदेश देते हुए कहने लगे, "क्या पवित्रशास्त्र में यह नहीं लिखा है, 'मेरा घर सब देशों के लोगों के लिए प्रार्थना का घर कहलाएगा'?
hi.R: यीशु मन्दिर के आँगन में गए। वहाँ जो लोग चीज़ें ख़रीद और बेच रहे थे, उन्हें वे बाहर निकालने लगे। उन्होंने पैसे बदलनेवालों की मेज़ें उलट दीं। उन्होंने कबूतर बेचनेवालों की चौकियाँ भी उलट दीं। \v 16 उन्होंने किसी को भी मन्दिर के आँगन में से होकर सामान ले जाने नहीं दिया। \v 17 फिर यीशु ने लोगों को उपदेश दिया। उन्होंने कहा, "पवित्रशास्त्र में परमेश्वर कहते हैं, 'मेरा घर ऐसा घर कहलाएगा जहाँ हर देश के लोग प्रार्थना कर सकें।'

uk.L: І, увійшовши до храму, {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} почав виганяти тих, що продавали й купували в храмі, і перекинув столи міняйлів і лавки тих, що продавали голубів, \v 16 і не дозволяв, щоб хтось проносив [якусь] річ через храм. \v 17 І {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} навчав і казав їм: «Хіба не написано: “Мій дім назветься домом молитви для всіх народів”?
uk.B: Він увійшов до храму й почав виганяти тих, хто там продавав і купував. Він перекинув столи міняйлів і лави продавців голубів, \v 16 і не дозволяв нікому проносити речі через храм. \v 17 Потім {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} навчав їх, кажучи: «Хіба Писання не каже: “Мій дім назвуть домом молитви для всіх народів”?
uk.R: Ісус увійшов на територію храму. Він почав виганяти людей, які там купували й продавали. Він перекинув столи, де люди міняли гроші. Він перекинув і лавки тих, хто продавав голубів. \v 16 Він не дозволяв нікому носити речі через храмові двори. \v 17 Тоді Ісус почав навчати людей. Він сказав: «У Писанні Бог каже: “Мій дім називатиметься домом, де люди з усіх народів можуть молитися.”

ja.L: そして神殿に入ると、神殿で売る者たちと買う者たちを追い出し始め、両替人たちの台と鳩を売る者たちの腰掛けをひっくり返された。\v 16 そして、だれかが神殿を通って器を運ぶことを許されなかった。\v 17 そして教え、彼らに言っておられた。「『わたしの家は、すべての国の民のための祈りの家と呼ばれる』と書かれているではないか？
ja.B: イエスは神殿の境内に入り、そこで売り買いしていた人々を追い出し始め、両替人の台や鳩を売る者たちの腰掛けをひっくり返された。\v 16 また、境内を通って物を運ぶことを、だれにもお許しにならなかった。\v 17 そして人々を教えて言われた。「『わたしの家は、すべての国の民の祈りの家と呼ばれる』と聖書に書いてあるではないか？
ja.R: イエスは神殿の境内に入られました。そして、そこで物を売り買いしていた人たちを追い出し始められました。お金を両替する人たちの台をひっくり返し、鳩を売る人たちの腰掛けもひっくり返されました。\v 16 また、だれにも、境内を通って物を運ばせないようにされました。\v 17 それからイエスは人々を教えて言われました。「聖書の中で、神はこう言っている。『わたしの家は、あらゆる国の人々が祈る家と呼ばれる。』

decisions.choice: money changers: they exchanged coins for the silver coins accepted at the temple
decisions.reason: Every Jewish man paid a half-shekel to the temple each year (Exodus 30:13). It had to be paid in coins of Tyrian silver, so pilgrims changed their money in the temple courts.

decisions.choice: doves: the offering of the poor
decisions.reason: The law allowed those who could not afford a lamb to offer two doves or pigeons (Leviticus 5:7; 12:8). Sellers supplied pilgrims with animals that would pass inspection.

decisions.choice: vessel: any container or goods
alternatives: the sacred vessels of the temple
decisions.reason: The word is general: a jar, a basket, a load. People used the temple courts as a shortcut, and Jesus stopped them.

decisions.choice: My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations: Isaiah 56:7
decisions.reason: In Isaiah 56:6-7 God promises that foreigners who hold to him will be brought to his holy mountain, and their offerings accepted. The trading likely took place in the outer court, the only part of the temple open to Gentiles.

decisions.choice: began to cast out: the same verb Mark uses for driving out demons
decisions.reason: The verb is a forceful one. Mark uses it for casting out demons (1:34, 3:15).

decisions.choice: driving out (B); throw out (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word used for demons; Balanced and Readable use everyday words for forcing people out.

decisions.choice: In the Scriptures God says
decisions.reason: Readable turns the question into a statement and says who speaks in Isaiah: the "my house" is God's.

decisions.choice: "đuổi ... ra" for "cast out"
decisions.reason: The meaning decision notes that Mark uses the same verb for driving out demons; "đuổi" is also the Vietnamese verb for that ("đuổi quỷ"), so the link is kept.

decisions.choice: "Nhà {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}" for God speaking in Isaiah 56:7; Readable introduces it with "Đức Chúa Trời phán"
alternatives: "Nhà Ta" with no span, as the English "My house" at the start of the quotation
decisions.reason: In Vietnamese "Ta" stands inside the phrase, not at its start, so it takes the deity_pronoun span as any pronoun for God does. "Phán" is kept for God speaking (style guide, Settled).

decisions.choice: "쫓아내다" (L, B); "내쫓다" (R) for cast out
decisions.reason: Mark uses the same verb for casting out demons (meaning decision); "쫓아내다" is the verb of the Korean Mark for that (3:15), so Literal and Balanced keep the link, and Readable uses the near form "내쫓다".

decisions.choice: "모든 민족" (L, B); "모든 나라 사람들" (R); "기도하는 집"
decisions.reason: "민족" is the plain modern word for ta ethne; "만민" is the older word of familiar versions. Readable says "people from every nation" in everyday words.

decisions.choice: echar fuera
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the phrase Spanish also uses for driving out demons, so the link Mark makes with that verb stays visible (meaning decision m5).

decisions.choice: chasser (every level)
decisions.reason: Mark uses the same verb for driving out demons (meaning decision). French "chasser" is the everyday word for both, so every level can keep the link that the English Balanced and Readable loosen.

decisions.choice: "Nyumba yangu" with a deity_pronoun span on "yangu"
decisions.reason: In the quotation God speaks of his house. The English "My" stands at the start of the quotation and is capitalised either way; the Swahili possessive comes after the noun, so it takes the deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: expulsar
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable leave "cast out", the word used for demons (m5). Portuguese "expulsar" is both the everyday word for forcing people out and the word for driving out demons ("expulsar demônios"), so every level keeps it and the echo is not lost.

decisions.choice: "ለአሕዛብ ሁሉ" (for all the nations) (L, B); "ከሕዝቦች ሁሉ የመጡ ሰዎች" (R)
decisions.reason: "አሕዛብ" is the Bible word for the nations other than Israel, and Isaiah 56:7 promises the temple to them; the Readable uses the plain "ሕዝቦች", as the style table has it.

decisions.choice: the quotation placed before "ተብሎ አልተጻፈምን?" (L), "... አይሉምን?" (B), "... ይላል" (R)
alternatives: "ተጽፏል" before the quotation, as Matthew 21:13 has it
decisions.reason: Mark asks a question ("Is it not written ...?"), and an Amharic question puts its verb at the end, after the words quoted.

decisions.choice: "изгонять" (L); "выгонять" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb used for driving out demons, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable use the everyday verb for forcing people out.

decisions.choice: "सब जातियों" (L); "सब देशों के लोगों" (B); "हर देश के लोग" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the style guide's "जातियाँ" for "the nations"; Balanced and Readable say "देश", since "जाति" also means caste (style guide 7b). Mark has "for all the nations", which Matthew 21:13 leaves out.

decisions.choice: "सर्राफ़ों" (L, B); "पैसे बदलनेवालों" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 21:12: the established word for money changers at Literal and Balanced, a plain description at Readable.

decisions.choice: "追い出す" (every level)
decisions.reason: Mark's forceful verb is the one he uses for casting out demons (m5). Japanese "追い出す" is the ordinary word for driving people out and also the word for casting out demons in this translation, so one verb keeps the link at every level without sounding strange; the English needs different words at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: "すべての国の民" (L, B); "あらゆる国の人々" (R)
decisions.reason: "The nations" is "諸国の民" in this translation; with "all" Japanese says "すべての国の民". Readable uses plain words for people from every nation, as Isaiah 56 means foreigners coming to pray (m4).

decisions.choice: a den of robbers: Jeremiah 7:11
decisions.reason: In his temple sermon Jeremiah warned people who did wrong and then came to the temple feeling safe. God asked whether his house had become a den of robbers, and warned that he would destroy it as he had destroyed Shiloh (Jeremiah 7:9-14).

decisions.choice: robbers: bandits, men of violence
decisions.reason: The word means a bandit or raider, not a dishonest trader. A den is where robbers hide and feel safe after their crimes. The charge is that the temple has become such a refuge, not only that prices were unfair.

decisions.choice: you: stated, in contrast with God's purpose
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out: God said one thing; you have made it another.

decisions.choice: a hideout for bandits
decisions.reason: Balanced uses plain words for Jeremiah's picture. Literal keeps the familiar phrase.

decisions.choice: "các người" for Jesus addressing those in the temple
decisions.reason: The style guide's form for Jesus speaking to crowds and opponents; it is firm without being rude. "Các con" is kept for the disciples.

decisions.choice: "강도들의 소굴" (L, B); "강도들이 숨는 곳" (R)
decisions.reason: "강도" is a man of violence, as the meaning decision says, and the word of the Korean John (10:1); "소굴" is the everyday word for a den of criminals; "굴혈" is archaic.

decisions.choice: una guarida de bandidos
decisions.reason: As in English: the robbers are violent men (meaning decision m2), and a hideout is where they go after their crimes. Literal keeps the familiar "cueva de ladrones".

decisions.choice: une caverne de brigands (L); un repaire de bandits (B); une cachette pour des voleurs (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a robber or bandit, a man of violence, not a petty thief (meaning decision), so Literal and Balanced say "brigands", "bandits". Literal keeps the cave of Jeremiah 7:11; Balanced says "repaire", a hideout; Readable uses the plainest words.

decisions.choice: "majambazi"
decisions.reason: The meaning note takes the word as bandits, men of violence. "Wezi" are thieves who steal quietly; "majambazi" are armed robbers, which is the sense, and the word is plain enough for Readable.

decisions.choice: "አደረጋችሁት" (you have made it)
alternatives: "እያደረጋችሁት ነው" (you are making it), as Matthew 21:13
decisions.reason: Mark has a perfect ("you have made it"), where Matthew has a present, so the Amharic of Mark uses the past and does not copy the Matthew wording; "ወንበዴዎች" is kept from Matthew.

decisions.choice: "強盗たちの洞穴" (L); "盗賊の隠れ家" (B); "強盗が隠れる場所" (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a cave or den, the place where bandits hide and feel safe (m1, m2). Literal keeps "cave"; Balanced and Readable say what the den is for, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ ἤκουσαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς, καὶ ἐζήτουν πῶς αὐτὸν ἀπολέσωσιν· ἐφοβοῦντο γὰρ αὐτόν, πᾶς γὰρ ὁ ὄχλος ἐξεπλήσσετο ἐπὶ τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And heard the chief priests and the scribes, and they were seeking how him they might destroy; they were afraid for of him, for all the crowd was astonished at the teaching of him.

en.L: And the chief priests and the scribes heard [it], and they were seeking how they might destroy {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; for they were afraid of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, for the whole crowd was astonished at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching.
en.B: When the chief priests and the scribes heard about this, they began looking for a way to do away with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They feared {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, since the whole crowd was spellbound by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching.
en.R: The leading priests and the teachers of God's law heard about this. They started looking for a way to kill Jesus. They were afraid of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because all the people were amazed at what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught.

vi.L: Và các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo nghe [điều đó], và họ tìm cách để diệt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}; vì họ sợ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì cả đám đông đều kinh ngạc về sự dạy dỗ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Khi các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy thông giáo nghe chuyện ấy, họ bắt đầu tìm cách trừ khử {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Họ sợ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì cả đám đông đều say mê lời dạy của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Các thầy tế lễ cả và các thầy dạy luật nghe biết việc này. Họ bắt đầu tìm cách giết Đức Giê-xu. Họ sợ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, vì mọi người đều kinh ngạc về những điều {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} dạy.

ko.L: 그리고 대제사장들과 율법학자들이 [그것을] 듣고, 어떻게 그분을 없앨까 하고 찾고 있었다. 그들이 그분을 두려워하였기 때문이다. 온 무리가 그분의 가르침에 놀라고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 대제사장들과 율법학자들이 이 일을 듣고, 예수를 없앨 방법을 찾기 시작했다. 그들이 예수를 두려워한 것은, 온 무리가 예수의 가르침에 감탄하고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.R: 대제사장들과 율법을 가르치는 선생들이 이 일을 들었다. 그들은 예수를 죽일 방법을 찾기 시작했다. 그들은 예수를 두려워했다. 사람들이 모두 예수께서 가르치시는 것을 듣고 놀랐기 때문이다.

es.L: Y lo oyeron los principales sacerdotes y los escribas, y buscaban cómo destruirlo; porque {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} tenían miedo, pues toda la multitud estaba asombrada de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza.
es.B: Cuando los jefes de los sacerdotes y los escribas se enteraron, empezaron a buscar la manera de acabar con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Le tenían miedo, porque toda la multitud estaba maravillada con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} enseñanza.
es.R: Los jefes de los sacerdotes y los maestros de la ley se enteraron de esto. Empezaron a buscar una manera de matar a Jesús. Le tenían miedo, porque toda la gente estaba asombrada de lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} enseñaba.

fr.L: Et les chefs des prêtres et les scribes [l’]apprirent, et ils cherchaient comment ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} feraient périr ; car ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} craignaient, car toute la foule était frappée d’étonnement par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} enseignement.
fr.B: Les chefs des prêtres et les scribes l’apprirent, et ils se mirent à chercher un moyen de {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} faire mourir. Ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} craignaient en effet, car toute la foule était saisie par {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} enseignement.
fr.R: Les chefs des prêtres et les spécialistes de la Loi ont appris ce qui s’était passé. Ils ont commencé à chercher un moyen de tuer Jésus. Ils avaient peur de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, parce que tous les gens étaient émerveillés par ce qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} enseignait.

sw.L: Na wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi wakasikia, nao wakawa wakitafuta jinsi watakavyomwangamiza; kwa maana walimwogopa, kwa sababu umati wote ulikuwa ukishangazwa na mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani na waandishi waliposikia habari hii, wakaanza kutafuta njia ya kumwua. Walimwogopa, kwa kuwa umati wote ulivutiwa sana na mafundisho {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Viongozi wa makuhani na walimu wa sheria walisikia habari hii. Wakaanza kutafuta njia ya kumwua Yesu. Walimwogopa, kwa sababu watu wote walishangazwa na mambo aliyofundisha.

pt.L: E os chefes dos sacerdotes e os escribas ouviram [isso], e procuravam como destruí-{{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}}; pois tinham medo {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, pois toda a multidão estava maravilhada com o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} ensino.
pt.B: Quando os chefes dos sacerdotes e os escribas souberam disso, começaram a procurar um jeito de acabar com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. Eles {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} temiam, porque toda a multidão estava encantada com o {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} ensino.
pt.R: Os chefes dos sacerdotes e os mestres da Lei ficaram sabendo disso. Eles começaram a procurar um jeito de matar Jesus. Eles tinham medo {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, porque todo o povo estava admirado com o que {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} ensinava.

am.L: የካህናት አለቆችና ጸሐፍትም ሰሙ፤ እንዴትም እንደሚያጠፉት ይፈልጉ ነበር፤ ይፈሩት ነበርና፤ ሕዝቡ ሁሉ በትምህርቱ ይደነቅ ነበርና።
am.B: የካህናት አለቆችና የሕግ መምህራን ይህን በሰሙ ጊዜ እርሱን የሚያስወግዱበትን መንገድ ይፈልጉ ጀመር። ሕዝቡ ሁሉ በትምህርቱ እጅግ ይደነቅ ስለ ነበረ ይፈሩት ነበር።
am.R: የካህናት አለቆችና የሕግ መምህራን ይህን ሰሙ። ኢየሱስን የሚገድሉበትን መንገድ ይፈልጉ ጀመር። ይፈሩት ነበር፤ ምክንያቱም ሕዝቡ ሁሉ በሚያስተምረው ነገር ይደነቅ ነበር።

ru.L: И услышали [это] старшие священники и книжники, и искали, как бы {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} погубить; ведь они боялись {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, потому что весь народ изумлялся {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} учению.
ru.B: Когда старшие священники и учители Закона услышали об этом, они стали искать, как бы {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} погубить. Они боялись {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, потому что весь народ был поражён {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} учением.
ru.R: Старшие священники и учители Закона услышали об этом. Они стали искать, как убить Иисуса. Они боялись {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}}, потому что все люди удивлялись тому, чему {{deity_pronoun:он|Он}} учил.

hi.L: और प्रधान याजकों और शास्त्रियों ने [यह] सुना, और वे ढूँढ़ने लगे कि उन्हें कैसे नाश करें; क्योंकि वे उनसे डरते थे, क्योंकि सारी भीड़ उनके उपदेश से चकित थी।
hi.B: जब प्रधान याजकों और व्यवस्था के शिक्षकों ने यह सुना, तो वे उन्हें मरवा डालने का उपाय ढूँढ़ने लगे। वे उनसे डरते थे, क्योंकि सारी भीड़ उनके उपदेश पर मुग्ध थी।
hi.R: प्रधान याजकों और व्यवस्था के शिक्षकों ने इसके बारे में सुना। वे यीशु को मार डालने का कोई रास्ता ढूँढ़ने लगे। वे उनसे डरते थे, क्योंकि सब लोग उनकी शिक्षा से हैरान थे।

uk.L: І почули старші священники й книжники, і шукали, як би {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} погубити; бо боялися {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, бо весь натовп дивувався з {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} навчання.
uk.B: Коли старші священники й учителі Закону почули про це, вони почали шукати способу, як позбутися {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}. Вони боялися {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, бо весь натовп був захоплений {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} навчанням.
uk.R: Старші священники й учителі Закону почули про це. Вони почали шукати, як убити Ісуса. Вони боялися {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}}, бо всі люди дивувалися з того, чого {{deity_pronoun:він|Він}} навчав.

ja.L: そして祭司長たちと律法学者たちは[これを]聞き、どのようにしてイエスを滅ぼそうかと探していた。彼らはイエスを恐れていたからである。群衆がみな、その教えに驚いていたからである。
ja.B: 祭司長たちと律法学者たちはこれを聞いて、イエスを亡き者にする方法を探し始めた。群衆がみなその教えに心を奪われていたので、イエスを恐れていたのである。
ja.R: 祭司長たちと律法の先生たちは、このことを聞きました。そして、イエスを殺す方法を探し始めました。人々がみな、イエスの教えにとても驚いていたので、イエスのことがこわかったのです。

decisions.choice: chief priests: the high priest and the leading priestly families who ran the temple
decisions.reason: The chief priests controlled the temple and its trade. Jesus had said they would reject him (8:31; 10:33).

decisions.choice: destroy: put to death
decisions.reason: The verb is used of killing, as in 3:6.

decisions.choice: for ... for: they feared him because the crowd was with him
decisions.reason: The two explanations follow each other: they wanted to kill him but feared him, and they feared him because the crowd hung on his words.

decisions.choice: the leading priests; the teachers of God's law
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain descriptions, as in earlier chapters.

decisions.choice: "các thầy tế lễ cả" for the chief priests at every level (whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The Protestant term the style guide settles, as in the Vietnamese John (11:47; 12:10); one term at every level so that readers recognise the group.

decisions.choice: "các thầy thông giáo" (L, B); "các thầy dạy luật" (R) for the scribes (whole chapter)
alternatives: "các thầy dạy luật của Đức Chúa Trời" (R)
decisions.reason: "Thầy thông giáo" is the established Protestant word, used in the Vietnamese John 8:3; "kinh sư" is the Catholic one. Readable says what they were, teachers of the law, as in 1:22.

decisions.choice: "대제사장들"; "율법학자들" (L, B), "율법을 가르치는 선생들" (R)
decisions.reason: The words of the Korean John (11:47; 8:3) and of the Korean Mark 3:22, kept through chapters 11-12.

decisions.choice: los principales sacerdotes (L), los jefes de los sacerdotes (B, R); los escribas (L, B), los maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The renderings of Spanish John 8:3, 11:47 and 12:10, used throughout Mark.

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres (every level); les scribes (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi (R)
decisions.reason: The French terms used in John (11:47; 8:3) and for the whole of Mark. "Les grands prêtres" would suggest several high priests at once; "les chefs des prêtres" names the high priest and the leading priestly families. "Scribes" is the traditional word; Readable says what they were, experts in the Law of Moses.

decisions.choice: "wakuu wa makuhani" (L, B), "viongozi wa makuhani" (R)
decisions.reason: The form used for the chief priests in John, at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what they were, as in 14:1 and 15:1. "Makuhani wakuu" is the plural of "high priest" in Hebrews, so it is kept for that title.

decisions.choice: "waandishi" (L, B); "walimu wa sheria" (R)
decisions.reason: The scribes were experts who copied and taught the law. "Waandishi" is the established church word, used in John 8:3, but to a new reader it means writers or journalists, so Readable says what they did, as the English Readable says "teachers of God's law". "Sheria" stays lowercase, as "law" does in English.

decisions.choice: "የካህናት አለቆች" (chief priests) at every level; "ጸሐፍት" (L), "የሕግ መምህራን" (B, R) for the scribes
decisions.reason: The scribes were teachers of the Law, not copyists, so Balanced and Readable say so; "የካህናት አለቆች" is already plain Amharic for the leading priests. The same holds through chapters 11 and 12.

decisions.choice: "старшие священники"; "книжники" (L), "учители Закона" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's book-wide terms: the Synodal plural "первосвященники" blurs the one high priest with the leading priests; the scribes were teachers of the Law.

decisions.choice: "प्रधान याजक" at every level; "शास्त्री" (L), "व्यवस्था के शिक्षक" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The book's terms (style guide section 6); Readable keeps "प्रधान याजक" where the English Readable says "leading priests". The same in 11:27.

decisions.choice: "律法学者たち" (L, B); "律法の先生たち" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable uses a plain description for the scribes, the teachers of the Law, through Mark. The chief priests stay "祭司長たち" at every level, a term readers meet often in the Gospels.

source.text: Καὶ ὅταν ὀψὲ ἐγένετο, ἐξεπορεύοντο ἔξω τῆς πόλεως.

records.literal_gloss: And when late it became, they were going out of the city.

en.L: And whenever evening came, they would go out of the city.
en.B: And each evening they went out of the city.
en.R: Every evening Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples left the city.

vi.L: Và mỗi khi chiều đến, họ đi ra khỏi thành.
vi.B: Mỗi buổi chiều, họ đi ra khỏi thành.
vi.R: Chiều nào Đức Giê-xu và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng rời khỏi thành.

ko.L: 그리고 저녁이 되면, 그들은 성 밖으로 나가곤 하였다.
ko.B: 날마다 저녁이 되면, 그들은 성 밖으로 나갔다.
ko.R: 저녁마다 예수와 제자들은 그 도시를 떠나 밖으로 나갔다.

es.L: Y cuando se hacía tarde, salían fuera de la ciudad.
es.B: Y cada tarde salían de la ciudad.
es.R: Cada tarde, Jesús y {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos salían de la ciudad.

fr.L: Et quand le soir venait, ils sortaient de la ville.
fr.B: Et chaque soir, ils sortaient de la ville.
fr.R: Chaque soir, Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples quittaient la ville.

sw.L: Na kila ilipokuwa jioni, walikuwa wakitoka nje ya mji.
sw.B: Kila jioni walitoka nje ya mji.
sw.R: Kila jioni Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} waliondoka mjini.

pt.L: E, quando se fazia tarde, saíam para fora da cidade.
pt.B: E, ao fim de cada dia, eles saíam da cidade.
pt.R: Todo fim de tarde, Jesus e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos saíam da cidade.

am.L: በመሸም ቁጥር ከከተማ ወደ ውጭ ይወጡ ነበር።
am.B: በየምሽቱም ከከተማዪቱ ይወጡ ነበር።
am.R: በየምሽቱ ኢየሱስና ደቀ መዛሙርቱ ከከተማዪቱ ይወጡ ነበር።

ru.L: И когда наступал вечер, они выходили из города.
ru.B: А каждый вечер они уходили из города.
ru.R: Каждый вечер Иисус и {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} ученики уходили из города.

hi.L: और जब साँझ होती, तो वे नगर से बाहर चले जाते थे।
hi.B: और हर शाम वे नगर से बाहर चले जाते थे।
hi.R: हर शाम यीशु और उनके चेले नगर से बाहर चले जाते थे।

uk.L: І коли наставав вечір, вони виходили за місто.
uk.B: І щовечора вони виходили з міста.
uk.R: Щовечора Ісус і {{deity_pronoun:його|Його}} учні залишали місто.

ja.L: そして夕方になると、[彼らは]いつも都の外へ出て行った。
ja.B: 夕方になると、一行はいつも都の外へ出て行った。
ja.R: 毎日夕方になると、イエスと弟子たちは都を出て行きました。

decisions.choice: whenever evening came, they would go out: something done each day
decisions.reason: The word for "whenever" with a past tense of repeated action usually describes a habit. It may also mean simply that evening came that day.

decisions.choice: they went out
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts have "he went out", speaking of Jesus alone. The SBLGNT reads "they", which includes the disciples, who are with him the next morning (11:20). Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: Readable says who went out.

decisions.choice: "성" (L, B); "도시" (R) for polis
decisions.reason: Jerusalem was a walled city, and "성 밖으로" says "out of the city" in a natural way; Readable uses the everyday word.

source.text: Καὶ παραπορευόμενοι πρωῒ εἶδον τὴν συκῆν ἐξηραμμένην ἐκ ῥιζῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And passing by in the morning they saw the fig tree having been dried up from [the] roots.

en.L: And passing by in the morning, they saw the fig tree withered from [the] roots.
en.B: Early the next day, as they went along, they saw the fig tree withered from the roots up.
en.R: The next morning, as they walked past, they saw the fig tree. It had dried up completely, all the way down to its roots.

vi.L: Và buổi sáng, khi đi ngang qua, họ thấy cây vả đã khô từ [tận] rễ.
vi.B: Sáng hôm sau, khi đi ngang qua, họ thấy cây vả đã khô héo từ rễ lên.
vi.R: Sáng hôm sau, khi đi ngang qua, họ thấy cây vả. Cây đã khô chết hoàn toàn, tận đến rễ.

ko.L: 그리고 아침에 지나가다가, 그들은 무화과나무가 뿌리째 말라 버린 것을 보았다.
ko.B: 이튿날 이른 아침에 그들이 길을 지나가다가 보니, 그 무화과나무가 뿌리째 말라 버려 있었다.
ko.R: 다음 날 아침에 그들은 그 무화과나무 옆을 지나갔다. 그 나무는 뿌리까지 바싹 말라 죽어 있었다.

es.L: Y pasando por la mañana, vieron la higuera seca desde [las] raíces.
es.B: A la mañana siguiente, al pasar por allí, vieron la higuera seca de raíz.
es.R: A la mañana siguiente, cuando pasaban por allí, vieron la higuera. Se había secado por completo, hasta las raíces.

fr.L: Et passant le matin, ils virent le figuier séché depuis [les] racines.
fr.B: Le lendemain matin, en passant, ils virent que le figuier avait séché jusqu’aux racines.
fr.R: Le lendemain matin, en passant par là, ils ont vu le figuier. Il était complètement sec, jusqu’aux racines.

sw.L: Na walipokuwa wakipita asubuhi, waliuona mtini umekauka kutoka mizizini.
sw.B: Asubuhi iliyofuata, walipokuwa wakipita njiani, waliuona ule mtini umekauka kuanzia mizizini.
sw.R: Kesho yake asubuhi, walipokuwa wakipita, waliuona ule mtini. Ulikuwa umekauka kabisa, hata mizizi yake.

pt.L: E, passando de manhã, viram a figueira seca desde [as] raízes.
pt.B: Na manhã seguinte, ao passarem por ali, viram a figueira seca desde as raízes.
pt.R: Na manhã seguinte, quando passaram por ali, eles viram a figueira. Ela tinha secado completamente, até as raízes.

am.L: በማለዳም ሲያልፉ በለሲቱን ከሥሯ ደርቃ አዩ።
am.B: በማግሥቱ ማለዳ በዚያ ሲያልፉ በለሲቱን ከሥሯ ጀምሮ ደርቃ አዩ።
am.R: በማግሥቱ ጠዋት በዚያ ሲያልፉ በለሲቱን አዩ። እስከ ሥሯ ድረስ ፈጽሞ ደርቃ ነበር።

ru.L: И, проходя мимо утром, они увидели, что смоковница засохла от корней.
ru.B: Рано утром на следующий день, проходя мимо, они увидели, что смоковница засохла до самых корней.
ru.R: На следующее утро они проходили мимо и увидели то инжировое дерево. Оно совсем засохло, до самых корней.

hi.L: और भोर को पास से जाते हुए उन्होंने अंजीर के पेड़ को जड़ों से सूखा हुआ देखा।
hi.B: अगले दिन सुबह जब वे उधर से जा रहे थे, तो उन्होंने देखा कि अंजीर का पेड़ जड़ों तक सूख गया है।
hi.R: अगली सुबह, जब वे उस रास्ते से जा रहे थे, तो उन्होंने अंजीर का वह पेड़ देखा। वह पूरी तरह सूख गया था, नीचे जड़ों तक।

uk.L: І, проходячи вранці, вони побачили смоковницю, що всохла від коріння.
uk.B: Рано-вранці наступного дня, проходячи повз, вони побачили, що смоковниця всохла від самого коріння.
uk.R: Наступного ранку, коли вони проходили повз, то побачили інжир. Він зовсім засох, аж до коріння.

ja.L: そして朝早く通りがかると、彼らはいちじくの木が根から枯れているのを見た。
ja.B: 翌朝早く、一行が通りかかると、あのいちじくの木が根元から枯れていた。
ja.R: 次の朝、そこを通りかかると、あのいちじくの木が見えました。木は根まですっかり枯れていました。

decisions.choice: withered: dried up, dead
decisions.reason: The word is used of plants that dry up and die (4:6).

decisions.choice: from the roots: completely, past any recovery
decisions.reason: A tree dried from its roots will not grow again (Job 18:16; Hosea 9:16).

decisions.choice: passing by in the morning: the next morning, on the same road
decisions.reason: They pass the tree again on their way into the city (11:12, 11:19).

decisions.choice: the next day (B); the next morning (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear which morning is meant.

source.text: καὶ ἀναμνησθεὶς ὁ Πέτρος λέγει αὐτῷ· Ῥαββί, ἴδε ἡ συκῆ ἣν κατηράσω ἐξήρανται.

records.literal_gloss: And having remembered Peter says to him, Rabbi, look, the fig tree that you cursed has withered.

en.L: And Peter, remembering, says to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Rabbi, look! The fig tree that {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cursed has withered."
en.B: Peter remembered and said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Look, Rabbi! The fig tree {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} cursed is all dried up."
en.R: Peter remembered what Jesus had said. He said, "Teacher, look! The fig tree {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put a curse on has dried up!"

vi.L: Và Phi-e-rơ, nhớ lại, nói với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Ra-bi, kìa! Cây vả mà Thầy đã rủa đã khô rồi."
vi.B: Phi-e-rơ nhớ lại và thưa với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}: "Thưa Ra-bi, xem kìa! Cây vả Thầy rủa đã khô héo rồi."
vi.R: Phi-e-rơ nhớ lại lời Đức Giê-xu đã nói. Ông thưa: "Thưa Thầy, xem kìa! Cây vả mà Thầy rủa đã khô chết rồi!"

ko.L: 그러자 베드로가 생각이 나서 그분께 말한다. "랍비, 보십시오. 선생님께서 저주하신 무화과나무가 말라 버렸습니다."
ko.B: 베드로가 그 일이 생각나서 예수께 말했다. "랍비님, 보십시오! 선생님께서 저주하신 무화과나무가 말라 버렸습니다."
ko.R: 베드로가 예수께서 하신 말씀이 생각났다. 그래서 말했다. "랍비님, 보십시오! 선생님께서 저주하신 무화과나무가 말라 버렸습니다!"

es.L: Y acordándose, Pedro {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dice: «Rabí, mira, la higuera que maldijiste se ha secado».
es.B: Pedro se acordó y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijo: «¡Mira, Rabí! La higuera que maldijiste se ha secado».
es.R: Pedro se acordó de lo que Jesús había dicho. Le dijo: «¡Maestro, mira! ¡La higuera que {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} maldijiste se ha secado!».

fr.L: Et Pierre, se souvenant, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Rabbi, regarde ! Le figuier que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as maudit a séché. »
fr.B: Pierre se souvint et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dit : « Rabbi, regarde ! Le figuier que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as maudit est tout desséché. »
fr.R: Pierre s’est souvenu de ce que Jésus avait dit. Il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a dit : « Rabbi, regarde ! Le figuier que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} as maudit est devenu tout sec ! »

sw.L: Na Petro, akikumbuka, anamwambia, "Rabi, tazama! Mtini ulioulaani umekauka."
sw.B: Petro akakumbuka, akamwambia, "Rabi, tazama! Mtini ulioulaani umekauka kabisa."
sw.R: Petro alikumbuka maneno ya Yesu. Akasema, "Rabi, tazama! Mtini ulioulaani umekauka!"

pt.L: E Pedro, lembrando-se, {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} diz: "Rabi, olha! A figueira que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} amaldiçoaste secou."
pt.B: Pedro se lembrou e {{deity_pronoun:lhe|Lhe}} disse: "Olha, Rabi! A figueira que amaldiçoaste está toda seca."
pt.R: Pedro se lembrou do que Jesus tinha dito. Ele disse: "Mestre, olha! A figueira que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} amaldiçoaste secou!"

am.L: ጴጥሮስም አስታውሶ እንዲህ ይለዋል፦ «ረቢ ሆይ፣ ተመልከት፤ የረገምካት በለስ ደርቃለች።»
am.B: ጴጥሮስም አስታውሶ «ረቢ ሆይ፣ ተመልከት! የረገምካት በለስ ደርቃለች» አለው።
am.R: ጴጥሮስ ኢየሱስ የተናገረውን አስታወሰ። እንዲህም አለው፦ «መምህር ሆይ፣ ተመልከት! የረገምካት በለስ ደርቃለች!»

ru.L: И, вспомнив, Пётр говорит {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}}: «Равви, смотри! Смоковница, которую {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} проклял, засохла.»
ru.B: Пётр вспомнил и сказал {{deity_pronoun:ему|Ему}}: «Равви, смотри! Смоковница, которую {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} проклял, совсем засохла.»
ru.R: Пётр вспомнил, что сказал Иисус. Он сказал: «Учитель, смотри! Дерево, которое {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} проклял, засохло!»

hi.L: और पतरस याद करके उनसे कहता है, "हे रब्बी, देखिए! वह अंजीर का पेड़ जिसे आपने शाप दिया था, सूख गया है।"
hi.B: पतरस को याद आया और उसने उनसे कहा, "हे रब्बी, देखिए! जिस अंजीर के पेड़ को आपने शाप दिया था, वह सूख गया है।"
hi.R: पतरस को याद आया कि यीशु ने क्या कहा था। उसने कहा, "हे गुरु, देखिए! जिस अंजीर के पेड़ को आपने शाप दिया था, वह सूख गया है!"

uk.L: І, згадавши, Петро каже {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}}: «Равві, глянь! Смоковниця, яку {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} прокляв, усохла.»
uk.B: Петро згадав і сказав {{deity_pronoun:йому|Йому}}: «Поглянь, Равві! Смоковниця, яку {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} прокляв, зовсім засохла.»
uk.R: Петро згадав, що сказав Ісус. Він сказав: «Учителю, поглянь! Інжир, який {{deity_pronoun:ти|Ти}} прокляв, засох!»

ja.L: そしてペトロは思い出して、イエスに言う。「ラビ、ご覧ください！あなたが呪われたいちじくの木が枯れています。」
ja.B: ペトロは思い出して、イエスに言った。「ラビ、ご覧ください！あなたが呪われたいちじくの木が、すっかり枯れてしまいました。」
ja.R: ペトロは、イエスが言われたことを思い出しました。そして言いました。「ラビ、見てください！あなたが呪われたいちじくの木が、枯れてしまいました！」

decisions.choice: cursed: called down harm on it
decisions.reason: Peter names Jesus' words of 11:14 a curse, a word spoken against something that brings about harm.

decisions.choice: has withered: a perfect, it dried up and stays dead
alternatives: is in the process of withering
decisions.reason: The tense describes a finished event with lasting result.

decisions.choice: Rabbi: a Hebrew title of respect for a teacher
